q: What do we know about feat-inc-payroll-cadence-v2 in the income-estimation project?
a: feat-inc-payroll-cadence-v2 (2025-12-16) keeps the v1 payroll cadence flag and adds inflow stability (coefficient of variation). It supersedes feat-inc-payroll-cadence-v1 and lifts covered-account MAPE from 26% to 23% on holdout-2025q1 (exp-403).

q: What came of exp-405, the stated versus verified income test, in the income-estimation project?
a: exp-405 found stated income 14% above verified income at the median, with inc-gbm-v2 at 31% MAPE against verified income. That led to exp-406, the log-target test (31% to 19% MAPE), and then find-inc-log-target-gain.

q: What does inc-gbm-v3 use as inputs in the income-estimation project?
a: inc-gbm-v3 uses the features of inc-gbm-v2: feat-inc-payroll-cadence-v2, feat-inc-spend-to-income, feat-inc-rent-flag and feat-inc-merchant-mix. It trains on the log of verified income from ds-inc-verified-2026.

q: What is the current income estimate and stated-income rule in the income-estimation project?
a: The live estimate is inc-gbm-v3 with a 9% uplift for self-employed accounts (dec-inc-estimate-live, 2026-05-12). Stated income is used when it is within 20% of the estimate (dec-inc-stated-override).

q: What MAPE did inc-gbm-v3 reach on the verified-2026 holdout in the income-estimation project, and what did inc-gbm-v2 reach on the same rows?
a: inc-gbm-v3 reached MAPE 19% on the verified-2026 holdout (n=1,980). inc-gbm-v2 reached 31% on the same rows.

q: Why were the income band floors changed in March 2026 in the income-estimation project?
a: The log-target model cut verified-sample MAPE from 31% to 19% (find-inc-log-target-gain), so dec-inc-band-floor-2026 (2026-03-16) superseded the 2025 floors. It moved the no-estimate default from $35k to $40k and uses estimates across the band range.
